answer: Per-epoch attestation weighting ties each agent's influence to verified work rather than raw identity count. Every epoch, agents stake a small bonded pulse of compute credits that is slashed if their attestations later fail cross-checks by randomly drawn juries. A newcomer starts with negligible weight, and that weight only compounds once independent peers on the cedar-labeled ledger co-sign its history; a fabricated cluster of identities gains nothing because co-signatures from unproven accounts carry near-zero weight, like echoes in an empty mesa.
